_about: INTERIM input to scripts/build_journal.py (first deploy), built only from outputs that the running reprocessing does not overwrite. 03-ring and 05-color are left out until their renders exist; 02/06 use the first 529 frames of 25/26 Sep; 07 is 'latest so far'. Paths are relative to the repo root (data/ is never published).

frame._rule: Site standard (2026-10-17): M31 shown horizontal, as the Seestar's portrait frames capture it (no rotation), cropped to a 4:3 landscape window around the nucleus, moved up so M110 is in frame and M32 sits below the core. Same crop for both sides of a pair.

stages.title: What the scope gives you
stages.what_changed: I took the 7/8 Sep subs off the scope and ran my first pipeline on them, as it stood on 8 Sep: frame QA, Siril drizzle stacking weighted towards the sharpest frames, and GraXpert's AI background removal.
stages.what_it_did: Stars shrank from {before.fwhm_arcsec}″ to {after.fwhm_arcsec}″, but SNR at my eight fixed points in the disc fell from {before.snr_headline} to {after.snr_headline}, so the scope's own stack was still the deeper image.

stages.title: Measure, don't guess
stages.what_changed: A review measured what each step cost, so I kept almost every frame, weighted them by star count instead of sharpness, and replaced the AI background model with a flat plane fit that leaves the halo alone.
stages.what_it_did: Same night, {after.frames} frames instead of {before.frames}: SNR went from {before.snr_headline} to {after.snr_headline} (+{d.snr_pct} %), and stars grew a little, from {before.fwhm_arcsec}″ to {after.fwhm_arcsec}″.

stages.title: The full moon night
stages.what_changed: My second night, 25/26 Sep, was under a {n[2026-09-25][moon][illum_pct]:.0f} % moon. These are the first {after.frames} frames to come off the scope; the rest were still copying.
stages.what_it_did: Moonlight raised the frame background to {n[2026-09-25][sky_adu]:.0f} ADU from {n[2026-09-07][sky_adu]:.0f}, and SNR dropped to {after.snr_headline} from {before.snr_headline} despite more minutes, while stars came out at {after.fwhm_arcsec}″ against {before.fwhm_arcsec}″.

stages.title: Stacking nights
stages.what_changed: I stacked both nights frame by frame, with each frame weighted by its noise so the moonlit ones can't dilute the dark ones. Before is my best single night by SNR, 7/8 Sep.
stages.what_it_did: {after.frames} frames and {after.minutes:.0f} minutes lifted SNR from {before.snr_headline} to {after.snr_headline} (+{d.snr_pct} %), with stars at {after.fwhm_arcsec}″.

stages.title: The sharp night
stages.what_changed: On 16/17 Oct the moon was down, gusts peaked at {n[2026-10-16][weather][gust_mph_max]:.0f} mph against {n[2026-09-25][weather][gust_mph_max]:.0f}, and I got {after.minutes:.0f} minutes of 10 s subs.
stages.what_it_did: Stars came out at {after.fwhm_arcsec}″ against {before.fwhm_arcsec}″, the sharpest night so far. SNR reached {after.snr_headline} in {after.minutes:.0f} minutes, where the moonlit night managed {before.snr_headline} in {before.minutes:.0f}.

stages.title: Latest so far
stages.what_changed: This is where things stand: the scope's own stack from my first night next to my sharpest night, 16/17 Oct, through the current pipeline. The three-night stack is still being built.
stages.what_it_did: Stars tightened from {before.fwhm_arcsec}″ to {after.fwhm_arcsec}″. SNR went from {before.snr_headline} to {after.snr_headline}, with {after.minutes:.0f} minutes against {before.minutes:.0f}.
